Subject: Staging handoff & accelerated GPU acceptance timeline

Sanjay —

Thanks again for yesterday's demo and for walking us through the evaluation use cases. Based on the throughput and latency targets you shared, I sketched an accelerated onboarding plan that gets your private deployment live behind your VPC and accepted by your engineering team in ~6 weeks. I attached a working MAP (Novus-MAP-v2.xlsx) and a quick capacity sizing CSV.

Highlights:
- Proposed GPU pool: 8x A100-80GB (3x hot nodes, 5x warm nodes) with 2x reserved for spike capacity.
- Eval window: 2 weeks of functional + 1 week of load and cold-starts.
- Acceptance criteria: 99th pct latency < 350ms for 75-token avg prompt at 30 qps, KV cache hit >= 40%.
- Procurement path: we can do a single-tranche reserved capacity or split into a 60/40 tranche to accelerate delivery.

Open asks for your team:
1) Can Novus commit to a 60% initial tranche (covers hot nodes + one warm tranche)?
2) Who will own SOC2 evidence ingestion (security contact)?
3) Any blackout dates for your infra team over the next 8 weeks?

If the above looks good I'll loop in Contracts/Procurement and drop a DocuSign link for the tranche schedule.

Best,
Rohan

>

> - SOC2 evidence: Priya (cc) will coordinate; she may ask for an SSO integration diagram and our expected audit window.

Good questions — short answers below and updated MAP attached.

1) Tranche/Delivery: yes — we can structure a 60/40 tranche. Initial tranche provisions hot nodes (3 hot) and 2 warm nodes that are sufficient for the functional eval. The second tranche ships the remaining warm nodes and spike capacity.

2) Product freeze Dec 7: we can schedule the hard cutover to private infra the week after your freeze (week of Dec 14). The evaluation can still run earlier in a hybrid topology — see fallback below.

3) Delivery slip fallback: we recommend a hybrid start: run the eval in our hosted environment with a matching kernel/config (same model + quantization profile). We can enable a dedicated hosted pool that mirrors the private config and then do a blue/green switch once physical GPUs arrive. That approach keeps latency profiles accurate and avoids blocking the acceptance window.

I attached an updated MAP with milestone dates and a short contingency column. If Priya can share the SOC2 evidence checklist I will loop our security engineer (Neha) to confirm exact artifacts and turnaround.

Next step: if budget sign-off comes back positive, Marissa will open the DocuSign tranche schedule and we can target the first tranche live for week of Dec 14.

Cheers,
Rohan
